note: Schema 2 (2026-07-29, docs/124 T1). Schema 1 declared caps that nothing inside `npm run check` enforced: its flash cap sat 23,328 bytes BELOW the image that actually shipped as 0.2.1, and `pcmBufferBytesMax` claimed 65,536 bytes against roughly 3.25 MiB of real PSRAM rings — a field no consumer ever read. Every number here now says where it comes from, and `npm run check:resource-budgets` proves the derived ones still match the source constants.

flash.policy: A budget, not a physical limit. Set with deliberate headroom over the shipped 0.2.1 image so unplanned growth is noticed early, while staying far below the partition ceiling. Raising it is allowed and expected; raising it silently is not.

partitionCeiling.source: partition table decoded from the shipped output/firmware/public-0-2-1/partitions.bin on 2026-07-29
partitionCeiling.note: app1 exists in the table but is unused: this appliance has no OTA (ADR-004). The 20,480-byte NVS partition is the whole settings store, which bounds the migration work in docs/124 T3.

shipped.source: release/release-0-4-1.json (appSizeBytes, sizeBytes, appSha256) — the record of the published 0.4.1 artifacts; the same figures are in output/firmware/, which is gitignored, so the measurement is recorded here to stay checkable in CI and in the public mirror

internalRam.enforcedBy: scripts/collect-firmware-evidence.mjs against the PlatformIO build summary; this figure needs a firmware build and is therefore outside `npm run check`
internalRam.note: Internal DRAM is the scarce resource for TLS, radio stacks and task stacks. shippedStaticBytes is the PlatformIO static RAM figure of the 0.4.1 build (output/firmware/s10-build-evidence.json staticRamBytes). The largest-free-block figure that matters at runtime lives in hardwareGatesPending.

psram.note: Derived from the compiled constants, never typed by hand. check:resource-budgets recomputes each entry from the source and fails if the manifest drifts.
psram.noteOnOtherConsumers: The logo store and the renderer also hold PSRAM. Until those are measured the audio total is a floor, not a budget.

hardwareGatesPending.note: TARGETS, NOT SOAK MEASUREMENTS. largestFreeBlockBytesMin now equals the gate the code enforces before a Bluetooth start (16 KiB in main.cpp); since 0.4.1 the firmware logs both sides of that boundary (start_admitted / start_refused), but no endurance soak has yet recorded them, so the figure is a code constant, not soak evidence. The earlier 32,768 was written before anyone costed a TLS session: two mbedTLS record buffers alone are about 33,434 bytes of internal DRAM, so neither value proves a TLS session fits next to A2DP. Treat these as the bar to clear in docs/124 stage 0 and stage 3, not as evidence.
